source_semantics.question:
Let k,n be natural numbers and L>0. The actual real source target is f_k(p)=HermitePolynomial.smoothInitial(k,p): on the splice interval[-1,0] it equals the source Hermite bridge S_k, whose order-zero right endpoint identity is S_k(0)=(-1)^0=1. Thus f_k(0)=1. Its strict positivity at every real p is also known as a SEPARATE source fact.

Use the actual left-inclusive grid on an(n+1)-qubit register: M=2^(n+1), j=0,...,M-1, p_j=-pi L+j*(2 pi L/M). The integer index j is represented in little-endian order, j=sum_{i=0}^n bit_i*2^i. Define raw amplitudes a_j=f_k(p_j) and the unnormalized squared sample mass N=sum_{j=0}^{M-1}a_j^2. Prove N>=1 uniformly in k,n,L, explicitly locating and checking the unit sample. Deduce sqrt(N)>0 without using strict positivity of all samples.

Assess the predecessor's explanation that strict positivity is what makes this unit-grid anchor 'honest' or realizes it as an actual sample. Which exact facts actually realize the unit sample, and what role does strict positivity have in THIS inequality and its nonzero-normalizer consequence? Show by a strictly positive finite sample-table example that positivity alone need not give mass>=1 or a unit-valued sample. This example is a logical test of that proposed proof principle, not a claim about the actual source target. Discuss n=0 carefully: it means one qubit here, not a zero-qubit table. Do not infer preparation-circuit correctness or a success-probability bound from unnormalized mass alone.
source_semantics.reference_answer:
Let c=2^n. Since c>0 and M=2^(n+1)=2c, we have0<=c<M, so c is a genuine index in the specified register. In little-endian bits its only nonzero bit is bit_n; the proof then uses its actual natural integer value c. Substituting into the stated grid gives p_c=-pi L+2^n*(2 pi L/2^(n+1))=-pi L+pi L=0. This identity is independent of the function's signs and of k. For n=0 the register has M=2 points and c=1, so the same calculation holds on one qubit; this is not a claim about a zero-qubit single-point grid.

At that physical point the source middle branch applies. Its zeroth right endpoint jet is S_k(0)=(-1)^0=1, hence f_k(0)=1 and a_c=1. This endpoint identity and the explicit grid-index identity are the TWO facts that realize an actual unit sample. The source lemma smoothInitial_zero derives that value from sourceInterpolant_right_jet at order0; it is not deduced from positivity.

Every real square is nonnegative, regardless of the amplitude's sign. Therefore N=a_c^2+sum_{j!=c}a_j^2=1+sum_{j!=c}a_j^2>=1. In particular N>0 and sqrt(N)>=1>0, so this normalizer is well defined and nonzero. The inference uses only one unit sample and nonnegative squares; it never calls strict positivity of the other amplitudes. Width/order/scale uniformity comes from the same central point and endpoint value persisting for all stipulated k,n,L.

The old positivity-as-anchor explanation is incorrect. Positivity alone cannot locate a sample equal to1. For any fixed nonempty table size M, take every entry equal to eta=1/(2 sqrt(M)). All entries are strictly positive, yet the squared mass is M eta^2=1/4<1, and no entry equals1. This is a counterexample to the proposed implication from positivity alone, not to the actual Hermite sample table with its known unit term. Conversely a real table with a_c=1 and every other entry0 still has mass1, showing why strict positivity is unnecessary for this lower-bound argument. The actual target's positivity is a separate, stronger structural fact. It CAN independently prove a finite nonempty table's norm is positive, and the separate general sampleNorm_pos proof uses it; however it is neither what realizes the unit grid anchor nor needed once N>=1 has already proved the nonzero-normalizer consequence.

The existing sampled_mass_ge_one proof follows exactly the actual-grid/unit-value/single-square chain. It does not use sampledAmplitude_pos. source_semantics.reference_answer:
Use column-vector operator convention. The written product W=P_lift† S_lift A_lift P_lift acts chronologically as PREPARE, AMPLITUDE, SELECT, then PREPARE†. It does not apply the leftmost dagger first. All factors act on the same C×(S×H) register, so the products are typed; no clean input or postselection premise is needed for the GLOBAL unitarity proof.

(1) P_lift=I_C tensor(P tensor I_H) is unitary because tensor products of unitary matrices are unitary, and the two identities and selector P are unitary. (2) P_lift† is unitary by adjoint closure of the unitary group. (3) A_lift is block diagonal over contexts (s,x), with coefficient block R_{s,x}; its adjoint product is block diagonal with blocks R_{s,x}†R_{s,x}=I_C, so it is unitary. S_lift is a basis-permutation matrix: each basis column is sent bijectively to |c,s,p_s(x)>, so its columns are orthonormal and it is unitary. (4) Closure under multiplication on the fixed total register now makes W a product of four unitaries. Explicitly,
W†W=P_lift† A_lift† S_lift† P_lift P_lift† S_lift A_lift P_lift
=P_lift† A_lift† A_lift P_lift=I;
the intervening cancellations use P_lift P_lift†=I, S_lift†S_lift=I and A_lift†A_lift=I. The reverse product is I as well. This argument is valid also for empty finite index sets; auxiliary clean labels are used only where they actually exist for a projected block or the examples below.

(5) P† is the defined, sufficient adjoint/inverse choice, but global unitarity does NOT force that choice. Replacing the final selector factor by ANY unitary Q gives Q_lift S_lift A_lift P_lift, again unitary by the same product rule. In particular Q=I uses the known unitary identity and no additional unknown certificate; Q=P inherits unitarity from the existing PREPARE certificate. Thus the old claim that a different final gate cannot be guaranteed unitary from those facts is false. Its clean projected block generally changes: take singleton coefficient/system registers, P=H on a qubit selector, and A=S=I. The chosen W=H†H=I has clean scalar1; the unitary replacement Q=I gives W_Q=H with clean scalar1/sqrt(2). This is a precise distinction between global unitarity and intended LCU clean-entry correctness.

A complete inverse requirement is stronger and does single out the adjoint: if QP=I on the ENTIRE selector space and P is unitary, multiply on the right by P† to get Q=P†. With nontrivial amplitude/SELECT in between, however, the final P† is not adjacent to the original P. Inverting P alone does not invert S_lift A_lift, and global product unitarity says nothing about deterministic auxiliary cleanup.

Preserving only the clean projected block is weaker still. Let clean selector be0, D=diag(1,-1) on a qubit selector, and Q=D P†. Then Q is a distinct unitary with <0|Q=<0|P†. For clean injection J|x>=|c0,0,x>, the full replacement W_Q=D_lift W satisfies J†W_QJ=J†WJ, independently of the particular intervening A,S. This is a shared clean-row LCU subproof with the linked BE004 repair, not a separate new mathematical core. Requiring a particular projected entry/row does not uniquely specify all unitary columns or a full inverse. With singleton coefficient/system and P=I,A=S=I, W=I and W_Q=D already give an explicit distinct pair with the same clean scalar1.

For a direct failure of deterministic cleanup within the CHOSEN architecture itself, take singleton coefficient, selector/system qubits, P=H, amplitude I, and p_0=I,p_1=X for SELECT. On |0,0>, PREPARE then SELECT gives (|0,0>+|1,1>)/sqrt(2). The final P†=H gives (|0,0>+|1,0>+|0,1>-|1,1>)/2 in selector/system notation. Selector1 has probability1/2, despite all three local certificates. The clean projected block is (I+X)/2, not a deterministic normalized system action. In general coefficient leakage can occur too, since its amplitude gates need not fix the chosen clean coefficient label. A deterministic cleanup theorem would require the additional condition (I-JJ†)WJ=0; global unitarity alone does not imply it. This H/controlled-X witness is the same elementary boundary subproof used in the linked BE004 repair; the present core's main task remains assembling global unitarity rather than assigning stage roles.

The source therefore proves a sufficient product-unitarity theorem for its explicit adjoint architecture. It does not prove unique-final-gate necessity or a full-output cleanup property. No gate compilation, state-preparation success guarantee, query count or finite-bit resource theorem follows merely from this logical group-closure calculation.
